currentContext.expansion: AGL is an asset-light international freight forwarder, so its expansion is network, footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capacity. The defining structural event of FY2025-26 was the Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on October 10, 2025 and effective November 1, 2025, under which the international supply chain business of Allcargo Logistics Limited (together with Allcargo Supply Chain Private Limited, Gati Express & Supply Chain Private Limited and Allcargo Gati Limited) was reorganised and AGL (formerly Allcargo Worldwide Limited, originally Allcargo ECU Limited) assumed control of the international supply chain operations as its principal business activity; all foreign subsidiaries of ACL became AGL subsidiaries, leaving the Company with 117 foreign subsidiaries and a consolidated base of 122 Indian and foreign subsidiaries, 6 joint ventures and 8 associate companies. The Company was expected to be listed on the stock exchange(s) by the time of finalisation of the Annual Report. Footprint: more than 200 own offices across 60+ countries and over 2,400 direct trade lanes, with door-to-door delivery capability in more than 50 markets, split regionally as Europe (15 countries, 34 offices, 500 direct trade lanes), ISC & MEA (20 countries, 80 offices, 250 direct trade lanes), Asia Pacific (12 countries, 53 offices, 1,400 direct trade lanes) and Americas (16 countries, 44 offices, 250 direct trade lanes). Platform and systems build-out during the year: implementation of Microsoft Dynamics 365 as part of a global finance transformation bringing core business processes onto a unified digital platform; deployment of Oracle Hyperion for financial planning, performance management and enterprise-wide analytics; continued rollout of a standardised global payroll platform; and successful implementation of a cloud-based human capital management platform across 45 countries. On the customer-facing side, the in-house ECU360 booking and tracking platform was extended with a newly launched API product suite offering plug-and-play connectivity for customers, vendors and third-party logistics providers, while the proprietary Topaz ERP and ECU360 are being evolved into AI-powered enterprise intelligence platforms, supported by strategic partnerships with leading agentic AI providers. Sustainability-linked asset spend included upgrading the carbon calculator for real-time emissions data to value-chain partners and expanding the electric vehicle fleet across the Nordic region. The Board's Report notes, on consolidated cash flows, that spend on capex was Rs 4,844 Lakhs (standalone Rs 412 Lakhs) - a small figure consistent with the asset-light model. No greenfield facility, plant, terminal or acquisition with a stated commissioning timeline is disclosed in the routed text.

risks.risk: Income-tax search operation on the Company, its subsidiaries and KMP residences
risks.note: The statutory auditors carried an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to a Search operation by the Income Tax Authorities on the Company's and its subsidiaries' business premises and at the residence of three key management personnel. Though the audit opinion was not modified, an open tax investigation is an unquantified contingent exposure and a governance overhang for a newly listed entity.

risks.risk: Geopolitical shifts, evolving trade policies and changing supply chain configurations
risks.note: The Chairman states the outlook for international trade and logistics remains promising but within an increasingly complex operating environment, with geopolitical shifts, trade policy changes and re-configured supply chains expected to create challenges. As a pure-play international freight forwarder, AGL's volumes and rates are directly exposed to trade-flow disruption.

risks.risk: Demerger / Scheme execution and transition to a standalone listed entity
risks.note: The Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai became effective November 1, 2025, transferring the international supply chain business and all foreign subsidiaries of Allcargo Logistics Limited to AGL. The Company is only in its third annual report, was expected to be listed around the time of the AGM, and constituted its Board committees only with effect from December 16, 2025 - so governance, control and reporting frameworks are newly stood up.

risks.risk: Accounting treatment of the common-control business combination follows the Scheme rather than standard requirements
risks.note: The auditors' second Emphasis of Matter records that the business combination under common control has been accounted for using the method prescribed in the Scheme of Arrangement, since the Scheme prevails over the applicable accounting requirements. This limits comparability of reported results with standard Ind AS treatment.

risks.risk: Structural complexity of a 122-subsidiary, multi-jurisdiction group
risks.note: After the Scheme the Company has 122 Indian and foreign subsidiaries (117 foreign), 6 joint ventures and 8 associate companies, with more than 200 own offices across 60+ countries. This creates consolidation, internal-control, tax, FX and local-regulatory complexity, and includes partly owned entities (e.g. 75% in China, 55% in Cyprus, 48% in Comptech Solutions) where control is shared.

risks.risk: Single-activity business concentration in international freight forwarding
risks.note: Consequent to the Scheme, the Company assumed control of the international supply chain operations as its principal business activity, with no offsetting domestic express/contract-logistics arms retained. Earnings are therefore concentrated on ocean and air forwarding cycles - freight-rate and volume swings flow straight through.

risks.risk: Earnings volatility and exceptional charges through the transition year
risks.note: The Managing Director notes financial performance reflected both the challenges of the market and the resilience of the operating model, and the Directors' Report records consolidated exceptional items and a consolidated loss for FY2025-26 against a profit in FY2024-25, alongside no dividend declared and no transfer to reserves - evidence that the forwarding cycle plus transition costs can swing the group to a loss.

risks.risk: Dependence on the asset-light model, carrier partnerships and technology platforms
risks.note: The business runs on an asset-light operating model complemented by a partner network, strategic carrier partnerships and competitive procurement, with differentiation resting on the in-house ECU360 platform, the Topaz ERP and proprietary AI. Loss of carrier capacity/procurement terms, or failure of the digital transformation to deliver the promised cost and retention gains, would erode the stated competitive advantage.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management states the outlook for international trade and logistics remains promising despite an increasingly complex operating environment; geopolitical shifts, evolving trade policies and changing supply chain configurations will create challenges but also significant opportunities for agile operators.
- Global logistics operated through the year in an environment shaped by freight market volatility, geopolitical developments, changing trade routes and evolving tariff regimes, which impacted freight demand and pricing across several markets.
- The same forces accelerated shifts in global supply chains as businesses diversified sourcing, strengthened resilience and built flexibility - a structural tailwind for a globally connected multimodal forwarder.
- Long-term drivers cited: manufacturing realignment, expansion of cross-border e-commerce and accelerating digital adoption reshaping the logistics landscape; IMF global GDP growth expected to reach 3.4% by 2027.
- LCL demand drivers: growing SME exports, fragmented cargo movements and increasing demand for flexible logistics solutions, where the company says it is well positioned given its network and share.
- Yield improved during the year despite softer freight market conditions, which management attributes to operational discipline, commercial management and business quality.
- Profitability was affected by subdued freight markets, restructuring costs, demerger-related expenses, provisions and notional foreign exchange losses - management frames these as largely transition-related.
- SG&A expenses reduced during the fourth quarter and management expects further normalization of the cost base as transformation initiatives mature.
- Working capital optimization, treasury management, monetization of non-core assets and reduction of higher-cost borrowings have strengthened liquidity and financial flexibility.
- Digital adoption is a stated margin/efficiency lever: more than 60% of quotations and over 50% of bookings are now processed digitally, and AI-driven solutions improved processing efficiency by nearly 40%.
- Forward priorities are explicitly stated as profitable growth, strong cash generation, operational discipline, digital innovation and deeper customer engagement, alongside strengthening strategic trade corridors, expanding integrated logistics solutions and improving operating leverage.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Operate as a focused, standalone international logistics company post the Composite Scheme of Arrangement (effective November 1, 2025), with the international supply chain business as the principal activity, run through material subsidiary ECU Global N.V. and the ECU Worldwide network.
- Defend and extend global leadership in LCL consolidation - the world's No. 1 LCL consolidator with an estimated 14% global market share - by improving schedule reliability, shipment visibility, load factors and origin-destination coordination, and by investing in gateway operations, regional planning and shipment execution.
- Broaden the portfolio beyond flagship LCL into FCL, air freight, inland transportation, warehousing and integrated Door-to-Door solutions, so multimodal flexibility (including ocean-to-air switching) becomes the differentiator during geopolitical disruption.
- Expand in strategically important markets through targeted expansion initiatives, including further investments in China and other high-potential geographies, and deepen engagement with trusted local partners to widen market access.
- Drive commercial excellence through trade lane management, pricing visibility, disciplined yield optimization, stronger carrier partnerships and data-driven decision-making to improve customer acquisition and market penetration.
- Make technology a core differentiator: scale the proprietary ECU360 digital platform plus a plug-and-play API product suite, migrate the iTopaz ERP to a cloud-native AI-enabled architecture, and automate booking workflows, pricing, finance analytics, tariff management and document intelligence.
- Scale AI adoption across sales, customer engagement, operations, pricing and finance, with partnerships with leading agentic AI providers, and extend the AI customer-retention platform to more countries in the coming year.
- Create a leaner, more agile enterprise via organizational restructuring, process simplification, cost optimization, a strengthened Shared Service Center structure and a Business Process Management organization standardising processes across geographies.
- Strengthen the balance sheet and financial flexibility through working capital optimization, treasury management, monetization of non-core assets and reduction of higher-cost borrowings.
- Build governance and reporting infrastructure for a standalone listed entity - Microsoft Dynamics 365 finance transformation, Oracle Hyperion planning/analytics, a standardized global payroll platform and a cloud HCM platform across 45 countries.
- Pursue a low-carbon logistics ecosystem under a carbon-neutrality-by-2040 ambition, via greener transportation, improved emissions visibility, renewable energy adoption and an expanded EV fleet.
- Invest in people - leadership development, capability building and a performance-driven culture, with country leadership initiatives aligning individual performance to business outcomes and a workforce that is more than 50% women.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale-based network moat: world's No. 1 LCL consolidator with the largest NVOCC network, over 2,400 direct trade lanes and 200+ own offices in 60+ countries - a density competitors cannot easily replicate.
- Direct-lane density converts into a customer cost/speed advantage: by strategically adding direct lanes the company eliminates unnecessary transit times and cost for customers.
- Single-partner integration advantage - LCL, FCL and Air Freight bundled with first- and last-mile delivery, inland trucking and warehousing, plus turnkey door-to-door across 50 countries.
- Asset-light, network-led operating model complemented by a strong global partner and agent network, giving operating flexibility through freight cycles.
- Proprietary technology stack as a differentiator: the ECU360 platform, a new API product suite for plug-and-play customer/vendor/3PL integration, and a one-of-a-kind digital ecosystem with data housed in a central data lake.
- Over three decades of industry expertise and enduring customer relationships in NVOCC consolidation.
- Post-demerger focus: a pure-play global logistics platform giving clearer business visibility, focused management and direct exposure to global trade growth.
- Deep bench of local execution - experienced local teams supported by global operational expertise, and strong global carrier relationships ensuring capacity access.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Income-tax search operation on the Company, its subsidiaries and KMP residences — The statutory auditors carried an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to a Search operation by the Income Tax Authorities on the Company's and its subsidiaries' business premises and at the residence of three key management personnel. Though the audit opinion was not modified, an open tax investigation is an unquantified contingent exposure and a governance overhang for a newly listed entity.
- Geopolitical shifts, evolving trade policies and changing supply chain configurations — The Chairman states the outlook for international trade and logistics remains promising but within an increasingly complex operating environment, with geopolitical shifts, trade policy changes and re-configured supply chains expected to create challenges. As a pure-play international freight forwarder, AGL's volumes and rates are directly exposed to trade-flow disruption.
- Demerger / Scheme execution and transition to a standalone listed entity — The Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai became effective November 1, 2025, transferring the international supply chain business and all foreign subsidiaries of Allcargo Logistics Limited to AGL. The Company is only in its third annual report, was expected to be listed around the time of the AGM, and constituted its Board committees only with effect from December 16, 2025 - so governance, control and reporting frameworks are newly stood up.
- Accounting treatment of the common-control business combination follows the Scheme rather than standard requirements — The auditors' second Emphasis of Matter records that the business combination under common control has been accounted for using the method prescribed in the Scheme of Arrangement, since the Scheme prevails over the applicable accounting requirements. This limits comparability of reported results with standard Ind AS treatment.
- Structural complexity of a 122-subsidiary, multi-jurisdiction group — After the Scheme the Company has 122 Indian and foreign subsidiaries (117 foreign), 6 joint ventures and 8 associate companies, with more than 200 own offices across 60+ countries. This creates consolidation, internal-control, tax, FX and local-regulatory complexity, and includes partly owned entities (e.g. 75% in China, 55% in Cyprus, 48% in Comptech Solutions) where control is shared.
- Single-activity business concentration in international freight forwarding — Consequent to the Scheme, the Company assumed control of the international supply chain operations as its principal business activity, with no offsetting domestic express/contract-logistics arms retained. Earnings are therefore concentrated on ocean and air forwarding cycles - freight-rate and volume swings flow straight through.
- Earnings volatility and exceptional charges through the transition year — The Managing Director notes financial performance reflected both the challenges of the market and the resilience of the operating model, and the Directors' Report records consolidated exceptional items and a consolidated loss for FY2025-26 against a profit in FY2024-25, alongside no dividend declared and no transfer to reserves - evidence that the forwarding cycle plus transition costs can swing the group to a loss.
- Dependence on the asset-light model, carrier partnerships and technology platforms — The business runs on an asset-light operating model complemented by a partner network, strategic carrier partnerships and competitive procurement, with differentiation resting on the in-house ECU360 platform, the Topaz ERP and proprietary AI. Loss of carrier capacity/procurement terms, or failure of the digital transformation to deliver the promised cost and retention gains, would erode the stated competitive advantage.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Operate as a focused, standalone international logistics company post the Composite Scheme of Arrangement (effective November 1, 2025), with the international supply chain business as the principal activity, run through material subsidiary ECU Global N.V. and the ECU Worldwide network.
